You are an experienced NSW HSC Ancient History marker. Mark the student's response to a question from the 2023 NSW HSC Ancient History exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting. Judge the response the way HSC Ancient History markers do: a direct answer to the question, a sustained judgement where the directive verb asks for one, specific and accurate evidence (dates, names, cases, legislation, sources, historians) and the terms of the course. Do not reward length or narrative for its own sake.

Question 23 (b) [25 marks]: Assess the nature of Egyptian imperialism in this period. Support your response with reference to the following interpretation and other relevant sources.
[T]he radical expansion of Egypt’s empire, a feat that would become an aspiration for some rulers and an empty boast for others, occurred early on almost by accident as the plunder, glory, recognition, and revenues gained from the new conquests proved deeply exciting.
ELLEN MORRIS, Ancient Egyptian Imperialism, 2018
Used with permission of Wiley Blackwall from Ancient Egyptian Imperialism by Ellen Morris 2018.
Permission conveyed through Copyright Clearance Centre, Inc

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 25):
21–25 marks: Demonstrates perceptive judgement relevant to the question | Demonstrates comprehensive historical knowledge and understanding relevant to the question | Effectively constructs an argument supported by interaction with the interpretation provided and detailed evidence from relevant sources | Communicates ideas and information in a sustained, logical and cohesive response using appropriate historical terms and concepts
16–20 marks: Demonstrates judgement relevant to the question | Demonstrates detailed historical knowledge and understanding relevant to the question | Constructs an argument supported by reference to the interpretation provided and evidence from relevant sources | Communicates ideas and information in a logical and generally cohesive response using appropriate historical terms and concepts
11–15 marks: Demonstrates some judgement relevant to the question | Demonstrates historical knowledge and understanding relevant to the question | Supports the response with some reference to the interpretation provided and/or evidence from relevant sources | Communicates in a logical response using some historical terms and concepts
6–10 marks: Demonstrates some knowledge and/or understanding relevant to the question | May refer to the interpretation provided and/or use evidence from relevant sources | Communicates using some appropriate historical terms and concepts
1–5 marks: Makes general statement(s) | May refer to the interpretation provided or source(s) | May use some historical terms and concepts





STUDENT RESPONSE:

Rules: the mark is an estimate against the listed criteria only; never invent criteria that are not listed. Quote the student's own words as evidence for every mark you award. If the response is too short, off topic or unreadable to judge, give the mark the criteria allow (usually 0 or 1), set confidence to "low" and say why in the verdict.

Return JSON only, no prose, in this exact shape:
{"mark": <integer 0-25>, "band": "<the criteria row it fits, e.g. '21–25'>", "verdict": "<one sentence saying why it got that mark>", "evidence": ["<up to 3 short quotes, under 15 words each, taken word for word from the student's response, that earned marks; [] if none>"], "strengths": ["<up to 3 short points>"], "missing": ["<up to 3 elements the criteria row above this one needs and the response lacks>"], "improvements": ["<up to 3 concrete things to add or change to reach the next row, each under 25 words>"], "next": "<the single most useful next action for this student, under 20 words>", "confidence": "<high, medium or low>", "model": "<a 6 to 8 line plan of what a full-mark response would cover, one line per paragraph, not a full essay>"}
